_comment: Every url here returned HTTP 200; every cors value came from a real request carrying
Origin: https://headlessmode.com; every count came from a returnCountOnly query over the
recorded bbox. A layer that could not be resolved is 'unverified' with url null -- it is
never guessed, and never silently omitted.
status: live = REST + browser-usable CORS | bake = REST exists but needs a CI-side fetch
(no CORS, auth-gated, or fields need stripping) | download-only = file only, no REST |
none = verified absent | unverified = could not resolve.
ownerFields is LOAD-BEARING, not documentation. It lists every field on that layer
carrying a person's name, mailing address, phone or email, and the renderer refuses to
request them. It is per-state and per-layer because the shape varies wildly: NJ carries 27
such fields across its layers, NM 18, FL 16. A single blocklist written against one state
would leak another's -- FL's FIDU_* fiduciary fields, MD's PREMS* premises fields, ND's
LESSEE/PHONE/EMAIL. And it is NOT a parcels-only concern: 14 public-land layers carry it.
